_metadata.description: Supplement timing and absorption interaction rules for optimal nutrient uptake

timing_rules.advice: Vitamin D is fat-soluble, and taking it with your largest meal may improve absorption - a small study saw blood levels rise by about half.
timing_rules.mechanism: Vitamin D is fat-soluble, so co-ingested dietary fat stimulates bile release and mixed-micelle formation that carry it across the intestinal wall. Mulligan and Licata 2010 measured a 56.7% mean rise in serum 25(OH)D after patients moved their usual dose to the largest meal of the day. The study was an uncontrolled cohort of 17 treatment non-responders, so the size of the effect should be read cautiously.

sources.label: Mulligan GB, Licata A - Taking vitamin D with the largest meal improves absorption and results in higher serum levels of 25-hydroxyvitamin D. J Bone Miner Res. 2010

timing_rules.advice: CoQ10 is fat-soluble and is best absorbed with fat in a meal.
timing_rules.mechanism: Coenzyme Q10 is highly lipophilic; co-ingestion with fat enhances micellar solubilization in the GI lumen and facilitates chylomicron-mediated absorption into the lymphatic system.

timing_rules.advice: Keep iron supplements at least 4 hours away from levothyroxine — iron can reduce levothyroxine absorption.
timing_rules.mechanism: Iron supplements can bind or adsorb levothyroxine in the digestive tract and reduce the amount absorbed. Current Synthroid labeling applies a 4-hour separation to iron supplements.

sources.label: DailyMed - SYNTHROID (levothyroxine sodium) tablets, section 17 Patient Counseling Information: do not take within 4 hours of iron and calcium supplements or antacids
Skelin M et al. — Factors Affecting Gastrointestinal Absorption of Levothyroxine: A Review

timing_rules.advice: Alpha-lipoic acid is better absorbed on an empty stomach. Taking it with food lowers peak blood levels by roughly 30 percent.
timing_rules.mechanism: The cited reference reports that food lowered peak plasma lipoic acid by about 30 percent and total plasma exposure by about 20 percent compared with fasting. It does not establish a specific number of minutes before a meal.

timing_rules.advice: Vitamin E is fat-soluble and the digestive tract needs fat to absorb it, so pairing it with a meal containing some fat is sensible.
timing_rules.mechanism: In a randomized four-way crossover study of eight healthy adults, a vitamin E capsule produced higher measured alpha-tocopherol concentrations with higher-fat meals than with a low-fat meal or water. NIH ODS also notes that the digestive tract requires fat to absorb vitamin E.

sources.label: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements — Vitamin E Fact Sheet
Jeanes YM et al. — The absorption of vitamin E is influenced by the amount of fat in a meal and the food matrix

timing_rules.advice: Keep calcium supplements at least 4 hours away from levothyroxine — calcium can reduce levothyroxine absorption.
timing_rules.mechanism: Calcium supplements can reduce levothyroxine absorption. Calcium carbonate did so in a seven-person pharmacokinetic study, and current Synthroid labeling applies a 4-hour separation to calcium supplements.

sources.label: DailyMed - SYNTHROID (levothyroxine sodium) tablets, section 17 Patient Counseling Information: do not take within 4 hours of iron and calcium supplements or antacids
Singh N et al. — The acute effect of calcium carbonate on the intestinal absorption of levothyroxine

timing_rules.advice: Higher-dose iron can cause nausea, constipation or stomach upset. Taking it with food can help minimize this.
timing_rules.mechanism: NIH ODS states plainly: 'High-dose iron supplements can also cause gastrointestinal effects, including gastric upset, constipation, nausea, abdominal pain, vomiting, and diarrhea. Taking iron supplements with food can help minimize these adverse effects.' Food can reduce iron absorption, so this is a tolerability tradeoff rather than an absorption optimisation, which is why it is actionability=optional.

sources.label: NIH ODS - Iron Fact Sheet for Health Professionals: taking iron supplements with food can help minimize gastrointestinal adverse effects
